name: Cognitive Overload
description: When the amount of information or demands exceeds your working memory capacity, causing mental fatigue, decision paralysis, forgetfulness, and reduced focus.

immediateActions.title: Brain Dump: Clear the Cache
instructions: Grab paper or open a blank note
Set a timer for 3 minutes
Write EVERY thought, to-do, worry, and reminder currently occupying your head
Do not organise, sort, or censor — just get it all out
After 3 minutes, review your list and circle only the ONE most urgent/important item
Move everything else to a 'later' list, calendar, or delegate where possible
Close the list and focus only on your one circled item

immediateActions.title: Sensory Cognitive Reset
instructions: Stand up from your desk or current position
Walk to a different room or outside if possible
Look at something 20+ feet away for 20 seconds (20-20-20 rule for eyes)
Shake out your arms and legs vigorously for 15 seconds
Take a drink of water slowly, noticing the temperature and taste
Take 3 deep 'lion's breaths': inhale through nose, exhale through mouth with a sigh
Return with a clear intention for the next 25 minutes

immediateActions.title: 2-Minute Priority Filter
instructions: List all tasks currently competing for your attention
Apply the '2-minute rule': anything that takes less than 2 minutes, do it NOW
From what remains, ask: What is the ONE thing that, if done, would make everything else easier or irrelevant?
That is your 'first frog' — do it next
Move 2 other items to 'today' slot, everything else to 'this week'
Close all other tabs and documents; only keep open what you need for the first frog

immediateActions.title: Overwhelm Triage: Star & Circle Method
instructions: Write down everything that currently feels stressful or overwhelming, one item per line
Place a star next to items with a real deadline within the next 24 hours
Place a circle next to items that are truly within your control right now
For starred+circled items, write ONE tiny next action you can take in the next 2 hours
For items you circled without a star, schedule one 15-minute slot later this week
For items you cannot control, cross them off: I release what I cannot change right now

immediateActions.title: 25-Minute Focus Sprint
instructions: Choose ONE single task before starting the timer
Remove all notifications: phone on silent, extra tabs closed
Set a timer for 25 minutes
If off-topic thoughts arise, write them quickly on a scratch note — do not act on them yet
When the timer ends, write exactly where you stopped so re-entry is instant
Take a 5-minute walk or stretch break before deciding to do another sprint

safetyGuidance: Cognitive overload is your brain telling you it has reached capacity — it is not a personal failure, it is a system signal. Chronic overload can worsen over time, so if you regularly feel mentally saturated, examine your workload boundaries and consider discussing capacity with your manager, team, or loved ones. Your brain has limits, and respecting them makes you more effective in the long run, not less.
